references_named: Mladen Stilinović, In Praise of Laziness (1993)
rationale: The mechanism enacts the idea with real precision: requestIdleCallback is the readymade, and the painting literally grows only when the browser confesses idle time. Concept and execution collapse cleanly (P1), the chance/order axis is legible (timing handed to the scheduler, layout strictly row-by-row), and the double-coding works — surface gag for the casual viewer, attention-economy critique for the literate one. The graceful fallback for browsers that refuse to admit idleness is a strong tonal move that turns a technical limitation into a conceptual statement. The work is materially distinct from the catalogue's attention-measurement pieces (1000 Hours of Staring, The Artist Is Present) by inverting the argument: it measures the absence of attention via CPU scheduling rather than presence via visibility/focus events.
reservations: The data plate with six metrics borders on over-building for P3's minimal-gesture mandate, though it serves the Haacke-style confession well. The theme of attention/idleness as medium has been visited in the catalogue, so the novelty sits in the specific mechanism (requestIdleCallback) rather than the territory.
revision_suggestion: Consider trimming the data plate to three or four metrics to tighten the minimal-gesture discipline, or make the plate itself subject to the same idle-gating so it only updates when the painting is being made.
